newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end firmer as rate fears wane.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end firmer as rate fears wane.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended firmer on Thursday, aided by declining interest rate hike fears and strong Canadian fundamentals.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index added 28.47 points to 6276.65. Trading was active at 94.9 million shares worth C$1.5 billion.

Toronto's influential banking sector rose more than one percent after North American investors decided that the chance of a U.S. interest rate hike remained low, said Dunnery Best, Midland Walwyn's director of private client investing.
U.S. April consumer prices rose 0.1 percent as expected, but the core rate rose 0.3 percent against forecasts of a 0.2 percent increase.

Best also credited Canada's strong fundamentals, underlined in comments by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen on Thursday. Thiessen said the solid outlook for profits was reflected in Toronto's climbing stock prices and he forecast a stronger Canadian dollar.
Eleven of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes rose, including banks, real estate, golds and oils. The three declining groups were conglomerates, transportation and media.
Advancing issues outweighed decliners 546 to 427 and 305 were flat.
In individual issues, shares in Gandalf Technologies Inc. tumbled 34 percent or 0.83 to 1.61 on 1.7 million shares.
Late on Wednesday, the networking firm reported that it was seeking additional financing after its major bank forgave a loan default but lowered Gandalf's credit facility.
Losses in the past two days wiped out the 150 percent gains Gandalf shares made on Tuesday.

Precision Drilling Corp. jumped 2.80 to 60. Analyst Best said that investors bet Precision might share the fate of Canada's Dreco Energy Services Ltd., snapped up on Wednesday by Houston-based National-Oilwell Inc. at a rich price.
Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd. rose 1 to 29.
